feedback.details: All 5 files pass the regex ^ADR-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*\.md$. Sequential numbering 0001-0005 with no gaps or duplicates. This is the strongest criterion in the sprint.

Two fundamental failures across all 5 files. (1) Extra H2 headings: The contract mandates exactly 4 H2 headings (## Status, ## Context, ## Decision, ## Consequences). Every file contains additional H2 headings: ## Related NFRs and ## Relationships in all 5 files, plus ## Diagram in ADR-0002 (line 46) and ADR-0003 (line 46). This violates 'No additional H2 headings allowed.' (2) Word count failures: Status sections in ADR-0002 through ADR-0005 contain only 1 word each ('Accepted' — e.g., ADR-0003:7, ADR-0004:7, ADR-0005:7). ADR-0001 Status has 55 words but still has the extra-heading violation. Context in ADR-0003 has only 27 words, below the 50-word minimum.

All files with mermaid code blocks (ADR-0002, ADR-0003) pass mmdc validation with exit code 0. Files without mermaid blocks (ADR-0001, ADR-0004, ADR-0005) pass vacuously — the contract states 'Every code block fenced with ```mermaid must pass validation.'

Multiple issues: (1) ADR-0003 container diagram has an orphan node — `printer` ('Print Service') at line 57 has an outbound edge to `phomemo` (line 72) but no inbound edge from any other container within the system subgraph. It is disconnected from the internal container graph. (2) ADR-0002 context diagram correctly has Person (gardener) and System (sys) nodes with labeled edges. (3) ADR-0003 has Container nodes and External nodes. However, ADR-0001, ADR-0004, ADR-0005 have no diagrams at all. (4) Edge labels in ADR-0002 use verbose format like 'Enters seed packet data via manual input' which is acceptable but could be more specific about protocol.

All ADRs contain NFR identifiers matching NFR-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{2} and all referenced IDs exist in nfr_catalog.json. However, the contract specifies 'a ## Related NFRs subsection' — implying it should be a subsection (H3) under an existing section, not a standalone H2 heading. Currently every file has '## Related NFRs' as a top-level H2 (e.g., ADR-0001:56, ADR-0002:36), which also violates the 'exactly 4 H2 headings' rule from the sections criterion. The cross-references themselves are valid.

Multiple markdownlint failures: (1) MD025 — Multiple top-level headings in ADR-0003:5, ADR-0004:5, ADR-0005:5 (YAML frontmatter title conflicts with H1 heading). ADR-0001 and ADR-0002 lack frontmatter so avoid this error. (2) MD022 — Missing blank lines around headings in ADR-0003 (lines 7, 10, 13, 23, 24, 31, 37, 43, 46), ADR-0004 (lines 7, 10, 21, 38, 39, 46, 52, 58), ADR-0005 (lines 7, 10, 21, 34, 35, 43, 49, 55). (3) H2 headings use Title Case ('Status', 'Context') instead of sentence case ('status', 'context') — the contract mandates 'H2 and H3 must be sentence case'. (4) Extra H2 headings violate MD024 (no duplicate headings) since ## Related NFRs, ## Relationships, ## Diagram appear across files but are not among the 4 required.

Two failures: (1) The contract requires 'A ### Relationships subsection must exist directly under ## Status.' In all 5 files, 'Relationships' appears as a standalone H2 (## Relationships) at the end of each file (e.g., ADR-0001:64, ADR-0002:42), not as an H3 subsection under ## Status. (2) The content is just 'None' without the exact required phrase format. The contract specifies 'Must use exact phrases: Supersedes ADR-XXXX, Superseded by ADR-XXXX, Relates to ADR-XXXX, or None.' While 'None' is technically one of the allowed phrases, the structural placement is entirely wrong.

Partial compliance: (1) All files contain 'We chose to' at the start of the Decision section — ADR-0001:27, ADR-0002:13, ADR-0003:14, ADR-0004:22, ADR-0005:22. This passes the opening phrase requirement. (2) MISSING: '### Alternatives Considered' list with ≥2 bullet points does not appear in ANY file. None of the 5 ADRs document what alternatives were evaluated. (3) MISSING: '### Trade-offs' subsection with ≥1 pro and ≥1 con versus each alternative does not appear in ANY file. While ## Consequences has ### Positive and ### Negative subsections, these are not the required '### Trade-offs' format that explicitly compares the selected option against each alternative. The Positive/Negative sections are generic consequences, not structured trade-off analysis.

overall_summary: Sprint 7 shows dramatic improvement from Round 1 (1.1/10 — zero files existed) to having 5 ADR files with valid naming, passing Mermaid syntax, and valid NFR cross-references. However, the delivery is fundamentally incomplete against the sprint contract. Every single ADR file fails the 'exactly 4 H2 headings' rule by including ## Related NFRs and ## Relationships as H2 headings instead of H3 subsections. All 5 files completely lack '### Alternatives Considered' and '### Trade-offs' subsections, which are core to the ADR decision record pattern. The '### Relationships' subsection is not placed under ## Status as required. Status sections in 4 of 5 files contain only 1 word, far below the 50-word minimum. The container diagram has an orphaned 'Print Service' node disconnected from the internal graph. Markdownlint errors (MD022, MD025) plague 3 of 5 files. These are not polish issues — they represent missing structural elements that are central to the ADR pattern's purpose of documenting decision rationale and trade-off analysis.
